rationale: Retain one Portland Natural Gas Transmission System record and correct its complete 2024 ownership transition. BlackRock Global Infrastructure Fund IV and North Haven Infrastructure Partners III each acquired a 50% indirect interest through Beehive Loop AcquisitionCo LLC when the US$1.14 billion sale closed on August 15, 2024. The prior direct owners, TC Pipelines and Énergir's Northern New England Investment Company, exited their 61.7% and 38.3% interests at closing. PNGTS remains an active standalone FERC-regulated pipeline; the later MSIP census task is the same canonical company and must not create a duplicate owner or PortCo.

companyFieldUpdates.description: Portland Natural Gas Transmission System is a standalone FERC-regulated natural-gas transmission business serving New England and Atlantic Canada. The approximately 295-mile system crosses New Hampshire, Maine and Massachusetts, connects with Canadian pipelines and has nearly 460,000 dekatherms per day of capacity. Its customers include utilities, energy marketers, industrial users and power generators. BlackRock- and Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners-managed funds announced the acquisition from TC Energy and Énergir on March 4, 2024 and closed it on August 15, 2024 for approximately US$1.14 billion including assumed notes. Regulatory evidence identifies BlackRock Global Infrastructure Fund IV and North Haven Infrastructure Partners III as equal 50% indirect owners through Beehive Loop AcquisitionCo LLC. The former owners' 61.7% and 38.3% direct interests ended at closing. PNGTS maintains a corporate office in Houston and an operating office in Lancaster, New Hampshire. No later company sale or signed pending exit was identified through August 23, 2026.

set.event: Portland Natural Gas Transmission System entered service as an interstate transmission link between Canadian supply and New England markets.
TC Energy and Énergir agreed to sell PNGTS to BlackRock- and MSIP-managed funds for approximately US$1.14 billion including US$250 million of assumed notes.
The sale closed, establishing BlackRock Global Infrastructure Fund IV and North Haven Infrastructure Partners III as equal 50% indirect owners through Beehive Loop AcquisitionCo LLC.
New Hampshire regulators approved the ownership transfer and documented the two acquiring funds' equal indirect interests.
A Federal Register notice documented continuing PNGTS operations and its Houston corporate office while the pipeline pursued a blanket-certificate project request.
